blocks.text: CRE:200–222 DETAILED REVIEW AND DELEGATED APPROVAL — CANONICAL

The Creation affordance block was reconsidered from first principles under the standing delegated authority. The review compared five genuinely different architectures per root, scored 45 candidates across 360 criterion values, routed 115 English concepts without forced atomization, passed all 18 canonical packet checks, passed all 24 complete Creation-family soundness checks, and passed the complete authority regression. All deterministic generated forms remained unchanged.

Approved architecture: CRE:2xx names substrate-neutral productive affordances. The inward triplet states one entity's capacity to form or modify a retained generative pattern; the outward triplet states a generative relation from one source toward one distinct prospective artifact; and the systemic triplet states multiple participants' capacity to generate one jointly constituted result in one shared production domain. The third trit changes only persistent, operative, or latent status.

CRE:200 — persistent internal pattern-forming capacity — A persistent capacity within one reference entity to form or modify a generative pattern while retaining it within that entity, independently of whether that capacity is presently operative.

CRE:201 — operative internal pattern-forming capacity — A capacity within one reference entity to form or modify a generative pattern while retaining it within that entity that is presently operative.

CRE:202 — latent internal pattern-forming capacity — A capacity within one reference entity to form or modify a generative pattern while retaining it within that entity that exists without being presently operative.

CRE:210 — persistent source-artifact generative relation — A persistent generative relation from one source toward one distinct prospective artifact that can enable the artifact to be brought into manifestation by productive transformation, independently of whether that relation is presently operative.

CRE:211 — operative source-artifact generative relation — A generative relation from one source toward one distinct prospective artifact that presently enables the artifact to be brought into manifestation by productive transformation.

CRE:212 — latent source-artifact generative relation — A generative relation from one source toward one distinct prospective artifact that exists without presently enabling the artifact to be brought into manifestation by productive transformation.

CRE:220 — persistent systemic co-generative capacity — A persistent capacity of multiple participants in one shared production domain to generate one jointly constituted result through coordinated productive transformation, independently of whether that capacity is presently operative.

CRE:221 — operative systemic co-generative capacity — A capacity of multiple participants in one shared production domain to generate one jointly constituted result through coordinated productive transformation that is presently operative.

CRE:222 — latent systemic co-generative capacity — A capacity of multiple participants in one shared production domain to generate one jointly constituted result through coordinated productive transformation that exists without being presently operative.

Design boundary: these roots do not silently encode the Creation entity, actual productive process, imagination, general agency, creator identity, authorship, ownership, provenance, originality, formal algorithm, physical medium, structural composability, resource sufficiency, quality, scheduling, probability, or modality. A latent affordance exists but is not operative; it is not unknown, merely possible, undeveloped, disputed, planned, scheduled, or future. Runtime [2]/num remains assertion-level uncertainty and never selects lexical latency.
